correctness.rationale: Natural order antisymmetry gives zerosumfreeness, while no zero divisors yields a Boolean support semiring homomorphism h(s)=1_{s!=0}. This inductively converts finite semiring truth support to ordinary FO satisfaction. Let phi_n be the finite classical extension-closed but not Sigma_n definable sentence from Dawar–Sankaran; psi_n is a disjunction of r copies. By uniform saturation, value(psi_n) is t if phi_n holds and 0 otherwise. Since each nonzero s<=t in natural order, 0<=t and extension-closed support makes psi_n semiring extension preserved. If semiring equivalent to a Sigma_n formula, testing canonical 0/1 annotations and applying h would make phi_n classically Sigma_n-definable, contradiction. For S_k operations a⊕b=min(k,a+b), a⊗b=min(k,ab), zero divisors are absent and k-fold positive sums equal k; S_2 is non-idempotent (1⊕1=2). Domain finiteness and nonemptiness are essential. Independently checked source proof steps and algebra, with no attempt to turn small finite source tests into the unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: The three-element capped-counting counterexample draws a sharp mathematical boundary between equal-sized semirings with different additive idempotence: min-max lattice has finite extension preservation, capped counting does not at any bounded prefix level. The uniform saturation-transfer lemma is a usable structural mechanism across a class of semirings, beyond a one-off numerical example.
